title: Cache resonance field notes - sampling rounds
content:
Goal: understand a recurring ~10–30s latency bump pattern during low-background QPS periods. Suspect: KV cache churn + heartbeat-triggered priming leads to cache "resonance" (periodic eviction/repopulation) that cascades into p95/p99 spikes for high-priority requests.

Notes to self (quick):
- Not a pure cold-start: baseline stays warm, but small oscillations in cache occupancy correlate with bursts.
- Hypothesis: low-rate background priors (background analytical queries) evict hot keys because of LRU TTL interaction combined with KV-shard rebalancing.
- Target: create reproducible micro-workload that surfaces resonance and measure effectiveness of small mitigations (cache pinning, jittered heartbeat, fractional pin-to-warm).

Environment / infra:
- cluster: dev-fleet-a (3x worker nodes with A100s)
- runtime: serving-runtime v1.9.2 (local dev build with additional telemetry)
- model: rwi-gpt-medium-512-quant-int8 (tokenizer: rwi-tok-v2)
- sequence length for runs: mean 120, 95th 340, max 512
- config toggles: kvcache=true, prefetch=true, batcher: dynamic (max_batch=32, batch_timeout_ms=10)
- loadgen: vegeta + custom prefix-replayer (scripts/kv-replay.py)
- measurement: EFK (elastic) + internal token/time breakdowns, p50/p95/p99 from logging and APM traces

Experiment matrix (summary CSV):
run_id,qps,background_qps,concurrency,cache_pin,heartbeat_jitter_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms
r1,60,0,8,false,0,18,82,210
r2,60,5,8,false,0,24,190,620  # small background causes big spikes
r3,60,5,8,true,0,20,90,235  # pin hot keys -> big improvement p95/p99
r4,60,5,8,true,200,9,32,78   # pin + jittered heartbeat -> best
r5,120,10,16,false,0,22,240,800  # saturating concurrency amplifies resonance
r6,120,10,16,true,200,16,88,260

Raw observations / charts (ASCII sketch):
- r2 timeline (60 qps + 5 bkg):
  time -->
  p99  800|        .        .     .             .        .   .
  p95  200| .  .  .  .  .        .     .       .  .   .
  p50   20|. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
  (spikes roughly every 12–20s, amplitude grows when concurrency queue > 12)

Key takeaways so far:
- Small background QPS (5–10 qps) that touches many cold-ish keys causes cache churn that leads to tail latency amplification for normal traffic.
- Cache pinning (explicitly keep top-2000 keys resident) reduces p95/p99 significantly in testbed. Implementation note: pinning must handle memory pressure gracefully.
- Heartbeat jitter (randomize priming/refreshes across nodes by 100–300ms) smooths periodic alignment that appears to amplify cache eviction waves.
- Batcher thresholds interact: larger batches (32) increase p99 under churn because KV lookups pile up and extend token latency; reducing max_batch or lowering batch_timeout mitigates tail but lowers throughput. There's a cost/latency tradeoff.

Open questions / next cheap tests:
- Does LFU hybrid eviction (pin top keys based on frequency) outperform naive pin-after-warm? quick test: enable frequency tracking for 10m and pin top-5k.
- Are rebalances (shard resync) happening correlated to our experiment times? Need to cross-check cluster autoscaler and shard-eviction logs (k8s events + routing service).
- Try background workload that reads same hot keys (helps) vs reads many random keys (hurts). Could we rewrite background jobs to be cache-friendly?
- Impact of quantized KV layout: int8 model halves model memory but increases kvcache footprint ratio — measure memory churn.

Quick mitigation plan (prioritized):
1) Short-term fast: add 150–300ms jitter to heartbeat/priming schedule across the fleet (low risk).
2) Medium-term: implement optional pin-top-N keys API + graceful demote under pressure (needs server changes + telemetry).
3) Operational: add a periodic "cache-occupancy" compass metric (percent hot-key resident vs expected) + alert when occupancy drops >20% for 30s.

Implementation notes (commands used):
- veg: vegeta attack -rate=60/s -duration=600s -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report -type=json > r2-report.json
- kv replay: python scripts/kv-replay.py --trace traces/seen_keys.log --rate 5 --pattern=zipfian
- telemetry: kql queries: summarize by 10s bucket p99_latency_ms where route="/v1/generate" and model="rwi-gpt-medium-512-quant-int8"

Things I should write up for the team:
- Short explainer doc for SRE/product: why small background jobs matter for tail latency (one-pager).
- PR draft: heartbeat-jitter implementation + config flags (default ON for dedicated clusters).
- Run a 24h soak with pin-top-N enabled to see regressions (memory pressure, GC, OOMs).

Misc notes / brain dump:
- Felt like "resonance" in signal processing: periodic forcing (background operations) couples with our natural eviction frequency -> amplitude increases. The key is de-synchronization (jitter) or changing the coupling (pinning).
- Also check client-side retry/backoff patterns: aggressive retries from SDK can worsen resonance if many clients retry simultaneously after a spike. Maybe randomize retry jitter at SDK level.

Next immediate steps (tomorrow):
- Implement heartbeat jitter flag locally and run r3/r4 replicas.
- Add a quick metric: cache-occupancy-percent (derive from kvcache index size vs pinned-set) and push to grafana.
- Post results to #eng-serving-runtime and tag Arjun/Maya for review.

Unresolved: exact memory overhead of pin-top-N for int8 quantized models in our runtime (need mem profiler).

End.
